This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game. Then it explains the idea behind it. It ends
with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. Every question on this page
has its answer: try first, then check.

## Key terms

{{< glossary dot-product perpendicular angle-between-vectors forward-vector field-of-view unit-vector normalization magnitude vector component >}}

## 3.1 One number from two vectors: the dot product

- Does the wind help a boat, or slow it down? The game needs one number.
- The **dot product** multiplies the matching components and adds them:
  a · b = a~x~ b~x~ + a~y~ b~y~. In 3D, add a~z~ b~z~ too.
- The result is a **number** (a scalar), not a vector. The order does not
  matter.
- A boat moves (1, 0) and the wind is (3, 1): (1, 0) · (3, 1) = 3. Positive,
  so the wind helps the boat.

![(1, 0) · (3, 1) = 1 × 3 + 0 × 1 = 3.](images/dot-steps.png){width=80%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The products (3 and 0) are only a middle step. The dot product is their sum:
**3**, not (3, 0).
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The dot product in GeoGebra"}
At geogebra.org/calculator, type `u = Vector((2, 3))`, `v = Vector((4, -1))`
and then `u * v`. Calculate (2, 3) · (4, −1) by hand. Do the two numbers
agree?

::: {.check}
2 × 4 + 3 × (−1) = 8 − 3 = 5. GeoGebra shows 5 too.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Compute it"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(3, 0)|(8, −3)|−1"}
The boat moves (1, 0). The wind is (3, 1). The dot product?
:   3

    Why: 1 × 3 + 0 × 1 = 3.

(2, 3) · (4, −1)
:   5

    Why: 8 + (−3) = 5.

(1, 2, 3) · (4, 0, −1)
:   1

    Why: 4 + 0 − 3 = 1: in 3D, add three products.

(−2, 5) · (3, 1)
:   −1

    Why: −6 + 5 = −1.

What kind of result does a dot product give?
:   one number

    Why: the products are added into one scalar.
:::
:::

## 3.2 In front or behind? The sign of the dot product

- A guard's **forward vector** f shows where it looks.
- The vector from the guard to the cat: d = C − D.
- f · d **positive**: the angle is less than 90°. The cat is in front.
- f · d **zero**: exactly 90°. The cat is exactly to the side: d is
  **perpendicular** to f.
- f · d **negative**: more than 90°. The cat is behind.
- The same test with the velocity: positive = moving towards the goal.

![The sign of f · d: in front, to the side, behind.](images/dot-sign.png){width=84%}

{{< sim file="sims/dot-lab.html" poster="sims/dot-lab.png" title="Dot Lab: two vectors, one number" height="640" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Dot Lab"}
In **Dot Lab**, drag the orange arrow until the dot product is positive,
then zero, then negative. Write the two vectors and the dot product each
time. Where is the orange arrow when the result is zero?

::: {.check}
Positive: in front (less than 90°). Zero: exactly at a right angle, to the
side. Negative: behind (more than 90°).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · In front or behind?"}
A guard dog at D = (2, 2) faces f = (1, 0). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="far away|above the dog"}
A cat at (5, 3). Where is it?
:   in front

    Why: d = (3, 1), f · d = 3: positive.

A cat at (0, 4). Where is it?
:   behind

    Why: d = (−2, 2), f · d = −2: negative.

A cat at (2, 6). Where is it?
:   exactly to the side

    Why: d = (0, 4), f · d = 0: a right angle.

The dot product of two vectors is negative. The angle between them is…
:   more than 90°

    Why: a negative sign means the arrows point more away than together.

A player at (1, 1) moves (−1, 2). The treasure is at (4, 5). Is the player moving towards it?
:   yes, the dot product is 5

    Why: to the treasure (3, 4); (−1, 2) · (3, 4) = −3 + 8 = 5.

Are (4, 6) and (−3, 2) perpendicular?
:   yes, the dot product is 0

    Why: −12 + 12 = 0 means a right angle.
:::
:::

## 3.3 How big is the angle?

- The dot product grows with the lengths. So first **normalize** both
  vectors.
- For two unit vectors, â · b̂ is a number from −1 to 1. It depends only on
  the angle.
- For any vectors: a · b ÷ (|a| × |b|).
- This number is the **cosine** of the angle (Lecture 6). For now, use the
  table:

| â · b̂ | 1 | 0.87 | 0.71 | 0.5 | 0 | −0.5 | −0.71 | −1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| angle | 0° | 30° | 45° | 60° | 90° | 120° | 135° | 180° |

![b̂ at four angles to â, with the value of â · b̂.](images/dot-angles.png){width=82%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
(3, 0) · (2, 0) = 6, but the angle is 0°. Divide first: 6 ÷ (3 × 2) = 1, so
0°.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Find the angle in Dot Lab"}
In **Dot Lab**, switch on **Unit vectors**. Make the angle 0°, 60°, 90° and
180°. Write â · b̂ each time and compare with the table.

::: {.check}
0° → 1; 60° → 0.5; 90° → 0; 180° → −1, as in the table.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · The angle"}
Use the table above. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="6°|0.5°|30°"}
Two unit vectors have the dot product 0.5. The angle?
:   60°

    Why: the table gives 0.5 → 60°.

Two unit vectors have the dot product −1. The angle?
:   180°

    Why: −1 means exactly opposite directions.

The angle between (2, 0) and (0, 7).
:   90°

    Why: the dot product is 0 + 0 = 0, so a right angle.

A guard faces (1, 0). The cat is in the direction (3, 4), so â · b̂ = 0.6. The angle?
:   between 45° and 60°

    Why: 0.6 is between 0.5 (60°) and 0.71 (45°).

(3, 0) · (2, 0) = 6. What is the angle?
:   0°

    Why: 6 ÷ (3 × 2) = 1, and 1 means 0°.
:::
:::

## 3.4 Can the guard see me? The vision cone

- A guard sees only a cone in front of it: its **field of view**.
- Example: 60° to each side of f, and 5 units deep.
- 60° gives the value 0.5 in the table. A smaller angle gives a bigger
  value.
- Seen when **both** are true: f̂ · d̂ ≥ 0.5 **and** |d| ≤ 5.

![The vision cone of a guard dog.](images/vision-cone.png){width=80%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A cat 50 units straight ahead has f̂ · d̂ = 1, but the dog does not see it.
Always check the distance too.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Draw a vision cone"}
On squared paper, mark a guard at (4, 4) facing (1, 0), and the points
(8, 7), (7, 8), (4, 9) and (1, 0). For each point, find d, |d| and f̂ · d̂.
Which points are seen (60° to each side, 5 units deep)?

::: {.check}
(8, 7): d = (4, 3), 5, 0.8: seen. (7, 8): d = (3, 4), 5, 0.6: seen. (4, 9):
d = (0, 5), 0: not seen. (1, 0): d = (−3, −4), −0.6: not seen.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Seen or not?"}
A guard at (1, 1) faces f = (1, 0). It sees 60° to each side and 5 units
deep. Choose the right answer. You can use an answer more than once.

::: {.match extra="behind, but seen"}
A thief at (5, 4): d = (4, 3), f̂ · d̂ = 0.8.
:   seen

    Why: 0.8 ≥ 0.5 and |d| = 5 ≤ 5.

A thief at (1, 6): d = (0, 5), f̂ · d̂ = 0.
:   not seen: too far to the side

    Why: 0 is less than 0.5: the thief is at 90°.

A thief at (−3, −2): d = (−4, −3), f̂ · d̂ = −0.8.
:   not seen: behind

    Why: a negative value means behind.

A thief at (11, 1): d = (10, 0), f̂ · d̂ = 1.
:   not seen: too far away

    Why: straight ahead, but 10 units is more than 5.

A thief at (4, −3): d = (3, −4), f̂ · d̂ = 0.6.
:   seen

    Why: 0.6 ≥ 0.5 and |d| = 5 ≤ 5.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Shadow Cat {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Shadow Cat** is a stealth game. A guard dog is at D = (6, 4) and looks
right: f = (1, 0). It sees a point at most 60° to the side (f̂ · d̂ ≥ 0.5)
and at most 5 units away. Bush A is at (10, 7), bush B at (9, 8) and bush C
at (6, 9). The fish is at (2, 1). The cat can hide only where the dog cannot
see it. Later the dog turns and looks up: f = (0, 1).

{{< sim file="sims/shadow-cat.html" poster="sims/shadow-cat.png" title="Shadow Cat: find the bush the dog cannot see" kind="game" height="680" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · The dog looks right"}
Shadow Cat: dog D = (6, 4), f = (1, 0), 60° to each side, 5 units deep.
Bushes A (10, 7), B (9, 8), C (6, 9). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(3, 4)|A|0.6"}
The vector from the dog to bush A.
:   (4, 3)

    Why: A − D = (10 − 6, 7 − 4).

f · d for bush B, with d = (3, 4).
:   3

    Why: 1 × 3 + 0 × 4 = 3.

Which bush is safe for the cat?
:   C

    Why: C has d = (0, 5): f̂ · d̂ = 0, less than 0.5. A (0.8) and B (0.6) are seen.

The cat goes for the fish at (2, 1). Is it in front of the dog?
:   no, behind

    Why: d = (−4, −3), f · d = −4: negative.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · The dog turns (harder)"}
Shadow Cat: dog D = (6, 4), now f = (0, 1). Bushes A (10, 7), B (9, 8),
C (6, 9). Fish (2, 1). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(0, −1)|−0.8|0"}
The value f̂ · d̂ for bush C, with d̂ = (0, 1).
:   1

    Why: (0, 1) · (0, 1) = 1: C is straight ahead now.

The value f̂ · d̂ for bush A, with d̂ = (0.8, 0.6).
:   0.6

    Why: 0 × 0.8 + 1 × 0.6 = 0.6.

Is any bush safe now?
:   no, all three are seen

    Why: A 0.6, B 0.8, C 1: all ≥ 0.5, all 5 units away.

The value f̂ · d̂ for the fish, with d̂ = (−0.8, −0.6).
:   −0.6

    Why: 0 × (−0.8) + 1 × (−0.6) = −0.6: behind the dog.

Which vector is perpendicular to the new f = (0, 1)?
:   (−1, 0)

    Why: (0, 1) · (−1, 0) = 0.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- The dot product a · b = a~x~ b~x~ + a~y~ b~y~ is one number.
- Positive: in front (less than 90°). Zero: perpendicular (90°). Negative: behind.
- For unit vectors, â · b̂ gives the angle (table: 0.5 → 60°, 0 → 90°).
- Vision cone: f̂ · d̂ ≥ 0.5 and |d| ≤ 5.
